newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME copper easier, other metals dull in Asia.
newsitem.headline: LME copper easier, other metals dull in Asia.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper prices were slightly easier during Asian trading hours on Wednesday from Tuesday's after-hours levels, while other metals were steady to weaker.

Traders said profit-taking hit copper, nickel and aluminium overnight after run-ups earlier this week to fresh nine-month highs, although the lower levels and the stronger yen had not lured much consumer interest during Asian hours.
At 0830 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper stood at $2,338/43 a tonne versus $2,342/44 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday and $2,350 at the afternoon kerb close.
LME three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,642/44 a tonne, little changed from $1,642/45 at 1900 GMT and $1,643 at the afternoon kerb close.
Nickel was quoted at $7,800/20. It closed down $235 at $7,850 at the afternoon kerb.
